families.name: Eyes open or closed cue
families.meaning: Tells the listener to shut or open their eyes to set up the practice.

families.name: Invitation to notice
families.meaning: Gently invites the listener to see, observe or check on something.

families.name: Counting breath rhythm
families.meaning: Counts the listener through a breath pattern to pace inhale and exhale.

families.name: Thoughts pass through
families.meaning: Reassures that thoughts and sensations arrive and leave without needing control.

families.name: Reassurance of safety
families.meaning: Tells the listener they are safe and fine, easing alarm.

families.name: Body part locating
families.meaning: Directs attention to a specific part or area of the body.

families.name: Breath through nose and mouth
families.meaning: Specifies the route the breath takes in and out.

families.name: Exhale cue
families.meaning: Prompts the listener to breathe out, often to release tension.

families.name: Pause to begin
families.meaning: Asks the listener to pause and start settling in.

families.name: Releasing and letting go
families.meaning: Encourages the listener to release effort, tension or control.

families.name: Keep breathing steadily
families.meaning: Encourages the listener to carry on with the breath without strain.

families.name: Reassurance of having enough
families.meaning: Tells the listener they already have what they need and nothing must be fixed.

families.name: Naming the anxious state
families.meaning: Names stress or feelings so the listener feels understood.

families.name: Stop trying to control
families.meaning: Eases the listener out of effort, control and forced change.

families.name: Permission to relax
families.meaning: Gives the listener explicit permission or ability to relax.

families.name: Focus on the breath
families.meaning: Directs attention toward the breath as the anchor of the practice.

families.name: Few deep breaths
families.meaning: Suggests taking a small set of deep breaths to start calming.

families.name: Return to body or breath
families.meaning: Brings attention back to the body or breath when the mind wanders.

families.name: Settle in comfort
families.meaning: Helps the listener get physically comfortable before starting.

families.name: Noticing sensations and feelings
families.meaning: Invites the listener to observe what they feel in body and mind.

families.name: Attention placement
families.meaning: Asks the listener to direct or bring their attention somewhere.

families.name: Sense of ease
families.meaning: Evokes a feeling of calm, ease and relaxation in the body.

families.name: Guide's own voice
families.meaning: Refers to the guide and their voice to build connection.

families.name: Present moment, not past or future
families.meaning: Redirects the listener away from past or future worry to now.

families.name: Acceptance of any experience
families.meaning: Tells the listener whatever they feel is acceptable, even if imperfect.
